defects.scenario: Log 3 sets at 205 lb x 9 reps, reload mid-session, reopen the day.
defects.expected: The completed sets read back as what was performed: 205 x 9.
defects.observed: They read 205 x 5 — the programme's prescribed reps, styled .mcl-ghost. Reproduced on all four rendering-engine families.
defects.root: Two restore paths had drifted. mc-setlog.js paintRestored() (cloud rehydrate) repainted values, cleared the ghost and set aria-checked. mc-session.js restoreSets() (the LOCAL reload path every refresh takes) set the tick class and nothing else, so the row kept build()'s prescription.
defects.impact: mc_setlog_v1 was always correct; only the screen lied. But the ghost is a live input, so unchecking and re-checking that row committed the prescription — 9 became 5 for real, and flowed into tonnage, session kcal, PR detection and banked history.
defects.fix: MCSetlogUtil.paintLoggedRow() is now the one repaint of an already-logged row, reading values from today's mc_setlog_v1 entry rather than from the DOM. Both restore paths call it. It also sets aria-checked, which restoreSets() never did.
defects.test: tools/test-mc-restore-fidelity.js — 100 assertions across 5 engine families, wired into verify.yml. Proven to fail on the pre-fix tree (44 failures).

defects.scenario: Log 3 sets on the largest multi-day page (26 days, 199 cards, 112 rows), reload.
defects.expected: The session record survives and the ticks come back.
defects.observed: mc_session_v1 is {} within a second and never returns — still {} and zero ticks twelve seconds later.
defects.root: This engine REBUILDS its day cards after the first paint. restoreSets() had already latched as done, so the ticked rows went with the old DOM; save(), firing on the rebuild's own mutations, read the fresh tick-free DOM as 'nothing in progress' and DELETED the record.
defects.impact: mc_setlog_v1 keeps the sets, so no history is lost — but the page reads as untouched and the athlete cannot see what they have already done. The tick marks and open-card position are gone for good.
defects.fix: Restore re-applies on every MC_SCAN (the shared 'cards just rendered' signal), re-entrant via a generation counter; and save()'s destructive branch is disabled while a restore is outstanding, staying disabled if restore exhausted its retries.
defects.test: Same gate, extended to the re-render engine — the only shape that exposes it. Proven to fail pre-fix with the diagnostic it is meant to give.

defects.scenario: Open a workout day on a fresh device and tap '🎯 Start Guided Mode'.
defects.observed: The tap lands on the first-run coaching hint instead. elementFromPoint at the button's centre returned .mc-hint-txt; Playwright's click times out, while a programmatic click starts guided mode correctly.
defects.root: MC_HINTS draws its one-time callout beside the control that triggered it, and on a workout page that places it over the Guided Mode entry. Nothing broke loudly — the hint's own outside-click handler simply dismissed it.
defects.impact: A first-time athlete taps the control, the tip disappears, and nothing else happens. Tapping again works; the hint is once-per-device and auto-dismisses after 6s, so the window is narrow.
defects.fix: .mc-hint is pointer-events:none with the ✕ opting back in. The same tap now reaches the control underneath AND still dismisses the hint.
defects.test: Verified three ways: the entry is reachable with the hint showing, a real tap starts guided mode, and the ✕ still dismisses.

defects.scenario: Restore a backup stamped version 3 that passes the app's own restore validation (transactions, budget and goals all arrays).
defects.expected: The backup restores and the app renders.
defects.observed: App.render() throws — "Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'targetDate')" and "(reading '2026-09')". If the payload also lacks `rules`, replace() itself throws and the restore fails outright.
defects.root: migrate()'s container backfills are version-GATED, so a payload that merely CLAIMS a version skips them. And the v<12 step iterates data.rules with no || [] guard — the only iteration in the function without one. migrate()'s own header describes exactly this failure mode and defends against it for six keys; the plan objects and month-keyed containers never got that treatment.
defects.impact: Reaches the household through every restore path — Store.replace() is what 'Restore backup', 'Restore cloud backup' and an incoming sync row all call. A broken app during the one operation reached for when something has already gone wrong.
defects.fix: An unconditional structural belt placed BEFORE the version steps. Idempotent and purely structural; defaults are deliberately EMPTY rather than seed()'s, so a restore never invents a house plan or a salary the household did not enter.
defects.test: 8 assertions in tests.html (run in CI by scripts/run-tests.mjs), proven to fail pre-fix — 3 failed / 330 passed — and 333/333 after.

defects.scenario: Reconcile every one of 318 recipes' stated calories against its own macros under Atwater (4/4/9).
defects.expected: Stated calories agree with the recipe's own protein/fat/carbs, within whole-gram rounding.
defects.observed: 8 macro profiles are 15–24% apart, every one overstating, every one in a 3/5/6-serving tier.
defects.root: Authoring, not code — the calorie figure and the macro figures come from different sources for these records.
defects.impact: A macro-conscious cook logging one of these gets a day total that does not reconcile with itself.
defects.fix: NOT FIXED, deliberately: which number is right is an authoring decision a checker may not infer, and §0.10 requires recording an ambiguous specification rather than changing behaviour arbitrarily.
defects.test: tools/validate-recipes.js now checks it with a named allowlist of the 8, so no NEW one can appear and a fixed one must be removed from the list. Proven both ways.

defects.scenario: Compare ingredient quantities between the smallest and largest authored tier, units normalised.
defects.expected: Scaling up never uses less of an ingredient.
defects.observed: 10 anomalies. Three REDUCE: shepherd's pie asks 3 garlic cloves at 2 servings and 2 at 4; garlic shrimp fried rice 1½ tbsp soy sauce → 1 tbsp; blackened chicken tenders ⅙ tsp garlic powder → ⅛ tsp. Seven jump 6–8× at a 2× scale.
defects.root: Authoring. Unit changes account for most apparent cases (8 oz → 1 lb IS double) — normalising units first removed 121 of 131 first-pass findings.
defects.impact: A cook following the larger version under-seasons.
defects.fix: NOT FIXED, deliberately — same reasoning as DEF-CB-01.
defects.test: Same validator, second named allowlist. A planted shrinking ingredient is caught; a stale entry fails with 'remove it from the list'.

defects.scenario: Independently re-check every scheduled run of .github/workflows/weekly-checkin.yml.
defects.expected: A weekly recap reaches trainees, as §7 of the Executive Summary promises.
defects.observed: 10 of 10 scheduled runs FAILED, 2026-07-12 through 2026-09-13. It has never once succeeded.
defects.root: The workflow guards on secrets.WEEKLY_CHECKIN_SECRET and exits 1 with a named error when it is unset. Every run died in 5–8 seconds, consistent with the guard rather than the curl.
defects.impact: A feature the product's own specification sells has never worked.
defects.fix: NOT CODE. Needs the repository secret set, plus the matching CRON_SECRET on the Supabase project. Neither can be done from this session, and neither should be.
defects.test: Re-verified independently this run via the Actions API — carried forward from the 2026-09-15 assessment, still open.
